Ahrefs
Data, SEO and Scraping
Research & evidence

Ahrefs is an SEO and marketing platform providing access to search, backlink, and competitor data through a REST API and a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI agents.

Access requirements

API and MCP access are included in paid Ahrefs plans (Lite, Standard, Advanced, and Enterprise), with usage metered by monthly API units and request row caps.

Example operations

• Analyze domain backlink profiles
• Research keywords and search intent
• Track keyword rankings over time
• Monitor brand visibility in AI search
• Audit site health and technical SEO issues

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

Description
Ahrefs provides tools for keyword research, competitor analysis, site auditing, and rank tracking.

Frequently asked questions Everything you wanted to ask about Ahrefs Plans, credits, data, AI search, integrations, security — answered. 48 of the most common questions, written for buyers, founders, and SEO teams. What is Ahrefs What is Ahrefs and what can it help me do? Ahrefs is an SEO and marketing platform that makes your business discoverable in search, AI, and beyond. It helps you research keywords, analyze competitors, audit your site for technical issues, track rankings, monitor your AI visibility, and build a stronger backlink profile. Its core tools (Site Explorer for competitor research, Keywords Explorer for keyword research, Site Audit for technical SEO, Rank Tracker for monitoring positions, and Brand Radar for AI visibility

What is Ahrefs MCP Ahrefs MCP lets AI agents securely access the Ahrefs API and enrich their answers with real Ahrefs data. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard that allows AI tools to connect with third-party APIs in a secure, consistent way. In our case, it connects AI tools with Ahrefs, enabling things like this: Connect to Ahrefs MCP Ahrefs provides a hosted MCP server that allows users with a Lite plan or higher to connect their Ahrefs account to supported AI tools. Once connected, your setup is synced and available across all devices linked to your personal or company account. info See our Ahrefs MCP use cases and prompt ideas for real examples and prompting tips to help you get the most from your MCP connection. Aircall
Communications and Messaging
Research & evidence

Aircall is an AI-powered customer communications platform providing telephony, messaging, and conversation intelligence features, with a developer platform that includes a REST API, webhooks, and an MCP implementation for AI assistants.

Access requirements

API access is included in all paid Aircall plans, though specific feature access and platform limits are determined by the plan tier. Access requires an Aircall account and the generation of API credentials.

Example operations

• List and manage users and teams
• Retrieve call transcripts, summaries, and sentiment data
• Start outbound calls
• Manage contacts and messaging templates
• Configure and manage webhooks for real-time event notifications

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

Aircall is a customer communications platform offering telephony, messaging, and AI-powered conversation intelligence.

pricing tier. The cost driver is the plan tier, which determines feature access (AI Assist, Analytics+, Power Dialer) and platform limits (team count, recording storage, analytics history). The Custom tier adds dedicated API developer support, suggesting deeper API needs may require a higher plan. Does Aircall have a GraphQL API? No. Aircall exposes a REST API (primarily v1, with v2 endpoints for select resources like Users) that communicates over HTTPS and returns JSON responses. There is no GraphQL endpoint. If you need a GraphQL interface for telephony data, you would need to build a wrapper layer on top of the REST API. What is the Aircall API rate limit? Productivity and Project Management
Research & evidence

Airtable is a cloud-based platform that provides a RESTful Web API for interacting with bases, tables, and records, supporting both read and write operations.

Access requirements

API access is available on all plans, with call limits varying by plan type (e.g., 1,000 calls/month for Free, 100,000 for Team, and unlimited for Business/Enterprise).

Example operations

• List records in a table
• Create a new base
• Read base schema
• Update records
• Manage record comments

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

Description
Airtable offers a Web API that allows users to interact with their bases, tables, and records.

Platform(s) Web/Browser, Mac app, and Windows app API record limits You can access the documentation for the Web API here , or directly from your base by clicking on the Help button in the upper right-hand corner while you are logged in on a laptop or desktop. Research & evidence

The Amazon Selling Partner API (SP-API) is a REST-based interface that enables developers to automate business operations for Amazon sellers and vendors, including order processing, inventory management, pricing updates, and shipment tracking.

Access requirements

Unresolved

Example operations

• Retrieve order details and status
• Update product pricing and inventory levels
• Manage shipment tracking information
• Retrieve financial transaction and tax reports
• Subscribe to business notifications

Integration assessment

Integration is feasible subject to documented requirements. Requirements or restrictions: Requires registration and approval in the Solution Provider Portal; Requires OAuth 2.0 authorization from a selling partner or self-authorization for private apps; Restricted operations require specific roles and Restricted Data Tokens (RDTs)

Seller A business that lists and sells their own goods on Amazon. Sellers fulfill orders directly or use Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA). Sellers can use the SP-API to automate catalog management, pricing updates, order processing, and inventory tracking. They can also access analytics to optimize their business performance. On this page API integration Copy for LLM All aspects of the Apify platform can be controlled via a REST API, which is described in detail in the API Reference . If you want to use the Apify API from JavaScript/Node.js or Python, we strongly recommend using one of the API clients: apify-client npm package for JavaScript, supporting both browser and server apify-client PyPI package for Python. You are not required to those packages - the REST API works with any HTTP client - but the official API clients implement best practices such as exponential backoff and rate limiting. Productivity and Project Management
Research & evidence

Asana is a project management platform that provides a RESTful API for programmatic access to tasks, projects, portfolios, and other work graph resources, alongside an official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI agent integration.

Access requirements

Asana offers free and paid subscription tiers, with API rate limits varying by plan; Enterprise tiers provide additional features like Service Accounts for org-wide access.

Example operations

• Create, read, update, and delete tasks
• List and update projects
• Manage custom fields and enum options
• Retrieve workspace and user information
• Manage attachments and time tracking entries

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Auth Methods
Asana supports OAuth 2.0 for user-delegated authorization and personal access tokens (PATs) for programmatic API access.

Overview A personal access token (PAT) contains your security credentials for the Asana platform. Much like an API key, generating a PAT allows you to access (i.e., make requests to) the Asana REST API upon successful authentication. A user can create many, but not unlimited, personal access tokens. When creating a token, you must give it a description to help you remember what you created the token for. 📘 PAT or OAuth? If you build an app, and the app needs to perform actions on behalf of users (e.g., getting data from Asana or making changes within Asana), you should use OAuth . Generating a PAT You can generate a personal access token from the Asana developer console . 📘 API explorer Your PAT also gives you access to the API explorer,

Personal access token
https://developers.asana.com/docs/personal-access-token

Asana’s API has several options for authenticating. The purpose of your app, who uses it, and its features will dictate the method of auth that’s best for your app. Here are the various authentication options and why you might want to use each of them. 📘 View only View only license users have limited access to the API. To check if a user has a view only license, use the get a workspace membership API endpoint. For more information on view only licenses, see this article in the Help Center . Personal access token A personal access token (PAT) is the quickest and simplest way to authenticate in the API. Auth Methods
Service Accounts provide long-lived programmatic access for enterprise-tier administrative tasks.

this guide. Service Account Similar to PATs, Service Accounts (SAs) are long-lived tokens that provide programmatic access to the API. Service Accounts are an Enterprise tier feature and can only be created by Asana super admins (see more about admin roles at Asana ). Unlike PATs, SAs provide complete access to all data within your Asana account, including private user data. As such, SAs are ideal if your app needs to have org-wide authorization. Some common use cases include: Creating periodic data backups Automating programmatic management of your Asana account. Description
Attio provides a public REST API for CRM data management.

Attio provides a public REST API which exchanges JSON over HTTPS. In this section, you will find guidance about working with the API. To get up and running, read our guide on how to authenticate requests . From there, feel free to explore other topics or jump straight to the reference documentation . Building an OAuth flow for your app Working within our rate limits Setting up and listening to webhooks Filtering and sorting record and entry API queries Paginating API responses If you’re looking to move beyond just the REST API and understand the Attio developer platform as a whole, you can find general documentation for Attio developers here . Overview - Attio Docs
https://docs.attio.com/rest-api/overview
Auth Methods
Attio supports OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow.

In order to make requests to the Attio REST API, you need to generate an access token. There are two ways to generate an access token: By implementing an OAuth 2.0 flow By generating an API key for your workspace You should prefer the OAuth 2.0 flow if building an app for multiple workspaces. If you are building an app for a single workspace, you can manually generate an API key to make requests on behalf of that workspace only. Generating access tokens OAuth 2.0 Attio implements the standard OAuth 2.0 specification , using the Authorization Code Grant Flow ( RFC 6749 section 4.1 ). You can find the reference for our OAuth authorize, token exchange and introspect endpoints here . If you would prefer a tutorial on how to implement an OAuth

• Configure store settings
• Query storefront scripts

Binance
Finance and Fintech
Research & evidence

Binance is a cryptocurrency exchange platform providing a comprehensive REST API and WebSocket interface for market data, trading, and account management.

Access requirements

Binance does not charge for API access itself; revenue is generated through trading commissions and tiered VIP fee schedules based on trading volume and BNB holdings.

Example operations

• Retrieve live market pricing and order book snapshots
• Fetch historical OHLCV candlestick data
• Execute spot and futures trading orders
• Query account balances and income history
• Manage sub-account API permissions

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

Description
Binance offers a REST API and WebSocket streams for accessing cryptocurrency market data and performing trading operations.

About README FAQ Tools The Binance server provides a Model Context Protocol (MCP) interface for Large Language Models (LLMs) to access real-time and historical cryptocurrency market data from Binance. It enables LLMs to retrieve live pricing, order book snapshots, historical OHLCV data, and exchange information, all without requiring API keys, facilitating the integration of cryptocurrency market insights into LLM applications. Key Features 01 Fetches historical OHLCV candlestick data for various timeframes 02 Provides exchange information including trading rules and symbol details 03 2 GitHub stars 04 Offers order book access for market depth analysis 05 Operates in read-only mode using Binance's public REST API 06 Provides live price

Auth Methods
Binance APIs use API keys passed via the X-MBX-APIKEY header and HMAC SHA256 signatures for secure endpoints.

limits on the API are based on the IPs, not the API keys. Endpoint Security Type Each endpoint has a security type that determines the how you will interact with it. API-keys are passed into the Rest API via the X-MBX-APIKEY header. API-keys and secret-keys are case sensitive . API-keys can be configured to only access certain types of secure endpoints. For example, one API-key could be used for TRADE only, while another API-key can access everything except for TRADE routes. By default, API-keys can access all secure routes. Security Type Description TRADE Endpoint requires sending a valid API-Key and signature. USER_DATA Endpoint requires sending a valid API-Key and signature.

https://binance-docs.github.io/apiAgent-API-EN/

accessed freely. TRADE Endpoint requires sending a valid API-Key and signature. USER_DATA Endpoint requires sending a valid API-Key and signature. USER_STREAM Endpoint requires sending a valid API-Key. MARKET_DATA Endpoint requires sending a valid API-Key. TRADE and USER_DATA endpoints are SIGNED endpoints. SIGNED (TRADE and USER_DATA) Endpoint Security SIGNED endpoints require an additional parameter, signature , to be sent in the query string or request body . Endpoints use HMAC SHA256 signatures. The HMAC SHA256 signature is a keyed HMAC SHA256 operation. Use your secretKey as the key and totalParams as the value for the HMAC operation. The signature is not case sensitive . Please make sure the signature is the end part of your query

Api Types
The Binance API is primarily a REST-based interface with support for WebSocket streams.

Docs » Home Rest API Information All endpoints return either a JSON object or array. Data is returned in ascending order. Oldest first, newest last. All time and timestamp related fields are in milliseconds. HTTP 4XX return codes are used for for malformed requests; the issue is on the sender's side. HTTP 429 return code is used when breaking a request rate limit. HTTP 418 return code is used when an IP has been auto-banned for continuing to send requests after receiving 429 codes. HTTP 5XX return codes are used for internal errors; the issue is on Binance's side. It is important to NOT treat this as a failure operation; the execution status is UNKNOWN and could have been a success. Any endpoint can return an ERROR; the error payload

Make your first signed and unsigned REST request Start with a plain curl GET to a public endpoint. A signed request adds your API key in a header, a timestamp, and an HMAC signature over the query string. Two base URLs matter here. Production Spot is https://api.binance.com , and the testnet from the previous section uses https://testnet.binance.vision . Keep the base URL in one configuration value so that switching environments never means editing request code. For endpoints with security type NONE, no key is needed. limits on the API are based on the IPs, not the API keys. Endpoint Security Type Each endpoint has a security type that determines the how you will interact with it. API-keys are passed into the Rest API via the X-MBX-APIKEY header. API-keys and secret-keys are case sensitive . API-keys can be configured to only access certain types of secure endpoints. For example, one API-key could be used for TRADE only, while another API-key can access everything except for TRADE routes. By default, API-keys can access all secure routes. Security Type Description TRADE Endpoint requires sending a valid API-Key and signature. USER_DATA Endpoint requires sending a valid API-Key and signature.

The Bright Data Partner connector lets you retrieve data from Bright Data’s scraping and data collection APIs directly within a Boomi process. You can integrate with the SERP, Dataset, Scraper, and Web Unlocker APIs to build end-to-end public web data workflows without leaving the Boomi platform. The Bright Data Partner connector is developed and maintained by Bright Data. Customer support is handled through the Boomi Support Portal, where tickets are triaged to Bright Data. Which object types are supported The connector supports the following object types, each accessed via the Execute action: Object Description Dataset Access marketplace datasets with filtering and snapshot retrieval Scraper Submit web scraping jobs and retrieve results

API Keys anytime in the Account settings . How do I relay the API key within a request? Here’s an example request: Sample Request curl --request POST \ --url https://api.brightdata.com/request \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{ "zone": "my_unlocker_zone", "url": "https://example.com/page", "format": "json", "method": "GET", "country": "us", "data_format": "markdown" }' The important part of this request is the Authorization header: 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' This <token> is your API key , which is required for every API request. authentication credentials at the workspace level Instead of entering API keys or bearer tokens manually in the Headers field each time, you can save your auth credentials in an HTTP API (Headers) account . Clay encrypts and stores the headers at the workspace level, making them reusable across any HTTP API enrichment column. Setting up an HTTP API (Headers) account from the enrichment panel: Open your Clay table and click Add enrichment . Search for and select HTTP API . In the enrichment panel, click the Select header account dropdown. Click + Add account . Auth Methods
ClickUp supports OAuth 2.0 for multi-user applications and personal API tokens for individual or testing purposes.

Authentication To use the ClickUp API, you must authenticate every request. For personal use, authenticate with your personal API token . For apps or integrations that other people use, use the OAuth flow , allowing users to authorize Workspaces for your app. Include the token in the Authorization header of your requests. Both methods ensure that you and your users only have access to the information permitted by ClickUp. 👍 View the OAuth endpoints. Personal Token Use a personal API token for individual or testing purposes. Personal tokens begin with pk_ . Add the token to the header: Authorization: {personal_token} . This is also needed to use the Try-It feature in the API docs. Generate or regenerate a Personal API Token Log in to

Research & evidence

Close is a CRM and sales platform that provides a REST API and an MCP server for building custom integrations, automating sales workflows, and connecting AI agents to CRM data.

Access requirements

API access is included in Close CRM plans, which are paid subscriptions. There are no separate per-request API fees or daily request quotas.

Example operations

• Create, read, update, and delete leads, contacts, and opportunities
• Log activities such as calls, emails, and SMS
• Manage sales workflows and sequences
• Query event logs for data changes
• Subscribe to webhooks for real-time notifications

The basis of the API is the GraphQL framework ↗︎ , created and open-sourced by Facebook. Overview Complete checklist of Cloudflare free tier limits: Workers 100K requests/day, Pages 500 builds/month, DNS 1000 records, R2 10GB storage. A quick guide to determine if your project fits within limits, with scenario decision tables and upgrade guidance. Key Takeaways CDN bandwidth is unlimited (for normal website traffic), but video and large file hosting is prohibited, with a 512MB per-file cache limit. Workers offers 100K requests/day with 30ms CPU per request, suitable for small APIs and SSR rendering. Daily visits >5000 may hit limits. Pages allows 20,000 files/site and 500 builds/month, sufficient for static blogs. Medium-sized content sites and team collaboration need monitoring. R2 provides 10GB storage with 1M writes/month.

analytics in the Cloudflare dashboard. GraphQL models a business domain as a graph using a schema. In the schema, there are logical definitions for different types of nodes and their connections (edges). These nodes are the datasets you use for your analytics. You write queries in GraphQL much like in SQL: you specify the dataset (table), the metrics to retrieve (such as requests and bytes), and filter or group by dimensions (for example, a time period). GraphQL differs from a traditional API: it has one single endpoint: https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/graphql You pass the query parameters as a JSON object in the payload of a POST request to this endpoint. You can use curl to make requests to the GraphQL Analytics API. Alternatively,

GraphQL Analytics API The GraphQL Analytics API provides data regarding HTTP requests passing through Cloudflare's network, as well as data from specific products, such as Firewall or Load Balancing. Network Analytics users also have access to packet-level data. Use the GraphQL Analytics API to select specific datasets and metrics of interest, filter and aggregate the data along various dimensions, and integrate the results with other applications. The basis of the API is the GraphQL framework ↗︎ , created and open-sourced by Facebook. There is an active developer community for GraphQL and powerful clients for running queries, which makes it easy to get started. Coda
Productivity and Project Management
Research & evidence

Coda is a productivity and project management platform that provides a REST API for interacting with documents, tables, pages, and formulas.

Access requirements

API access is managed via API keys generated in Coda account settings, which can be configured for read-only or read/write access.

Example operations

• List and filter documents
• Read and write page content in HTML or Markdown
• List and modify table rows
• Trigger button columns in tables
• Manage user permissions for documents

Integration assessment

Unresolved

Supporting claims

Description
Coda is a productivity platform that allows programmatic interaction with documents, tables, and pages via its API.

Coda API Migration Guide We recently announced ⁠ a new, stable release of the API, Version 1. Per our deprecation policy for the beta API, please migrate to the Version 1 API within 30 days of our deprecation notifications, that is, by August 21, 2020 . Version 1 of the API will be supported for at least the next 6 months (through January 15, 2021) and we will give at least 3 months notice before making any breaking changes on or after that date. Migration should generally be straightforward. The core change is to use v1 in your API urls instead of v1beta1 . For example, the endpoint to list documents is now https://coda.io/apis/v1/docs instead of https://coda.io/apis/v1beta1/docs . If you use Google Apps Script, see the Google Apps Script

Specifically: Page content can now be read or written in either HTML or markdown format. When updating a page, you can replace the page content or append to it. We’ve added new endpoints for creating pages and for exporting pages. Creating a page To create a page, send a POST request to the endpoint https://coda.io/apis/v1/docs/{docId}/pages . You can optionally include metadata like the page name, subtitle, icon, cover image, and parent page. You can also set the initial content of the page at the same time, specified as HTML or Markdown, or a URL to use as the source of an Embed page. Migration ⁠ for details. There are a handful of breaking changes that may require your attention. Breaking Changes Endpoints for views have been removed and merged with endpoints for tables Previously, you would use a separate endpoint to list and modify views than you would to list and modify tables. We have simplified the API to no longer require separate endpoints. You can now pass a view id to all table endpoints. For example, previously, to list all the rows in a view, you would use this view-specific endpoint: https://coda.io/apis/v1beta1/docs/<docId>/views/<viewId>/rows In the v1 API, you will instead pass that view id to the shared /tables/ endpoint: https://coda.io/apis/v1/docs/<docId>/tables/<viewId>/rows There also used to be

Copper
CRM and Sales
Research & evidence

Copper is a CRM platform designed for Google Workspace that tracks contacts, deals, and projects, offering a RESTful Developer API for custom integrations.

Access requirements

Full API access is restricted to the Business plan; lower tiers like Basic and Professional do not include full API access.

Example operations

• Create and manage contact records
• Retrieve and update deal information
• Manage project tasks
• Subscribe to webhook events
• Query and modify user records

Integration assessment

Integration is feasible subject to documented requirements. Requirements or restrictions: Full API access requires a Business plan subscription; API key generation is restricted to administrator users

• Full API access requires a Business plan subscription
• API key generation is restricted to administrator users

Supporting claims

Description
Copper is a CRM built for Google Workspace that tracks contacts, deals, and projects.

Copper: a CRM that lives inside Gmail and Google Workspace, with a REST API and webhooks Updated Nov 8, 2026 Last checked Oct 31, 2026 Agent score 3/4 Read as Markdown In short Copper is a CRM built to run inside Gmail and Google Workspace, tracking contacts, deals and projects without manual entry. Its RESTful Developer API includes webhook subscriptions and OAuth 2.0, and admins generate API keys under Settings > Integrations > API Keys. Copper has no official MCP server, so agents call the REST API directly. Good to know: Only admins can generate API keys, and the pricing page does not say which plans include API access, so confirm before buying. It is built for Google Workspace and is a poor fit for Microsoft 365 teams. The community

Auth Methods
Copper supports API key authentication for individual users and OAuth 2.0 for partner integrations.

Authentication ¶ There are two ways to access the Copper Developer API: API keys and OAuth2.0 . API Keys are suitable for individual users, while OAuth2.0 is the preferred approach for partner integrations. API Keys ¶ The Dev API uses token based authentication. You have to include the token in the header of every request, along with the email address of the user who generated the token. Users can hold multiple valid tokens at the same time. Admins can see all user generated tokens and generate new ones. To generate an API token, in the Copper web app go to System settings > API Keys and click the 'GENERATE API KEY' button. Copper allows you to label each key for its unique purpose. You'll need to generate an API key to make an API

Overview - Copper Developer API
https://developer.copper.com/introduction/authentication.html

Authentication via OAuth2.0 ¶ 1. Introduction ¶ You can now access the Copper Developer API via OAuth2.0 . This authentication method is an alternative to Copper's legacy API Keys , and is particularly well-suited for third-party integrations looking to create a seamless and secure link between their users and Copper. OAuth2.0 offers several advantages over the API Key flow: Authentication is open to all users, not just administrators No need to generate and copy API keys from Copper to your application Readily available client libraries help with smooth integration 2. Auth Methods
Datadog supports OAuth 2.0 for authorization.

explicit consent once and client credentials can be securely stored. This grant type allows applications to securely obtain a unique authorization code and exchange it for an access token that enables them to make requests to Datadog APIs. The authorization code grant flow consists of three steps: The application requests authorization from a user to access a set of Datadog scopes. When a user clicks Authorize , the application obtains a unique authorization code . The application exchanges the authorization code for an access token , which is used to access Datadog APIs. Use the PKCE extension Proof key for code exchange (PKCE) is an extension of the OAuth2 authorization code grant flow to protect OAuth2 clients from interception

Access Details
Discord enforces a global rate limit of 50 requests per second for bots, with additional per-route buckets and resource caps.

Discord API reference Every Discord API limit, in one table 107 documented limits 10 groups 2026-08-20 last verified Last verified Aug 20, 2026 against Discord Developer Docs - Rate Limits Discord enforces limits at four layers and a bot has to respect all of them at once. The REST layer has a global ceiling of 50 requests per second per bot plus per-route buckets whose size is only revealed in response headers. The gateway (the WebSocket that delivers events) caps how many payloads you may send per minute, how often you may identify, and how many guilds one connection can serve before sharding is mandatory. Payload limits govern what fits in a message: 2,000 characters of content, 10 embeds, 6,000 combined embed characters, 10

Discord API Rate Limits 2026: 50 req/s, Gateway, Embeds

Messenger Platform limits › Microsoft Teams Bot Framework limits › Slack API limits › Telegram Bot API limits › WhatsApp Cloud API limits › Frequently asked questions What is the Discord API rate limit for bots? Two layers. Globally, a bot may make 50 requests per second across all endpoints. Separately, each route has its own bucket whose size Discord does not publish; you read it from the X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining headers on every response, and X-RateLimit-Bucket tells you which routes share a bucket. Exceeding either returns HTTP 429 with retry_after in seconds. Interaction callback endpoints are exempt from the global limit. How long can a Discord bot message be? 2,000 characters of content. Ecwid by Lightspeed Ecwid by Lightspeed is a multi-channel e-commerce platform that lets merchants launch a storefront and sell across websites, social media (Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, Pinterest, Snapchat), online marketplaces, and in-person via point-of-sale. The platform handles centralized inventory and order management, automated marketing, payments, shipping, tax, and domain management. The Ecwid REST API exposes products, categories, orders, customers, payment and shipping methods, and storefront settings using OAuth 2.0 authentication with public (read-only) or private access tokens. Ecwid REST API allows you to access and manage any store data, payment and shipping methods, and storefront settings. We use OAuth 2.0 authorization simplified for single-store customizations, JSON-formatted data, and a clear structure. Please note that our REST API has rate limits . We accept up to 600 requests per minute per token . If you exceed the limit, all subsequent requests will be ignored with an error 429 and a "Retry-After": N header (number N is a cooldown) . If more requests continue to come from a non-working token, Ecwid will block it for much longer after 20 requests per minute or a total of 600 requests with non-working tokens per IP. Ecwid API also supports gzip encoding through the "Accept-Encoding": "gzip" header. Get

Auth Methods
Ecwid uses OAuth 2.0 for public app authentication and supports bearer tokens for API requests.

All requests to Ecwid REST API require an access token . Ecwid uses OAuth 2.0 to provide secure access to the store data for public apps. If you customize your own store, however, you can skip OAuth and easily get an access token for your store. This guide provides a walkthrough of a basic Ecwid API interaction, specifically, retrieving store profile information. To gain a deeper understanding of Ecwid API objects and their connections, refer to the API reference. Ecwid REST API allows you to access and manage any store data, payment and shipping methods, and storefront settings. We use OAuth 2.0 authorization simplified for single-store customizations, JSON-formatted data, and a clear structure. Please note that our REST API has rate limits . We accept up to 600 requests per minute per token . If you exceed the limit, all subsequent requests will be ignored with an error 429 and a "Retry-After": N header (number N is a cooldown) . If more requests continue to come from a non-working token, Ecwid will block it for much longer after 20 requests per minute or a total of 600 requests with non-working tokens per IP. Ecwid API also supports gzip encoding through the "Accept-Encoding": "gzip" header. Get

Firecrawl
Data, SEO and Scraping
Research & evidence

Firecrawl is a web data extraction API designed for AI agents, providing capabilities to search, crawl, map, and scrape web content into LLM-ready formats like Markdown, structured JSON, and screenshots.

Access requirements

Firecrawl offers a free tier with limited credits and paid subscription plans (Hobby, Standard, Growth, Scale, Enterprise) based on monthly credit consumption, with options for annual billing.

Example operations

• Scrape web pages into Markdown or JSON
• Crawl entire websites recursively
• Search the web and extract content
• Map all URLs on a website
• Interact with pages to click elements or fill forms

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Firecrawl is a context API for AI agents that transforms web data into structured formats like Markdown and JSON.

flow with resource=https://api.firecrawl.dev/ . Your app gets an fco_ access token that works on the REST API in place of an API key, plus an fcr_ refresh token. Each connection gets its own key. Your app never sees it, and deleting another key in the dashboard doesn’t affect the connection. The connection is listed under Connected apps in Settings , where the user can revoke it. Refresh tokens rotate and work once. Reusing an old refresh token revokes the whole connection. The full flow is in OAuth for apps . No API key (keyless) These REST endpoints work without an API key: /v2/scrape , /v2/search and /v2/parse (including /v2/parse/upload-url ) /v2/scrape/{jobId}/interact /v1/scrape and /v1/search On Firecrawl Cloud, the research,

gathering powered by AI. Alexandria Find and run structured data tools from third-party providers. Base URL All requests use the following base URL: https://api.firecrawl.dev Authentication Requests need an Authorization header with your API key, except on the keyless endpoints described below: Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR-API-KEY You can find your API key in the Firecrawl dashboard . A few endpoints, including /v2/scrape , /v2/search and /v2/parse , also work without a key, with limits. To call them keyless, leave the Authorization header out entirely, because a header with an empty token returns 401 . See No API key (keyless) for the full list. To let users connect their own Firecrawl account to your app instead, use OAuth for apps .

The Freshworks Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables AI tools like Cursor and Claude to securely connect and interact with Freshdesk. Research & evidence

Front is a customer communication platform that provides a Core API, Plugin SDK, and Channel API to enable custom workflows, UI extensions, and integration with external systems.

Access requirements

API access is included in Front plans, but specific rate limits apply based on the plan tier (Starter, Professional, Enterprise). Additional API rate limit capacity can be purchased as an add-on.

Example operations

• Syncing CRM data to Front contacts
• Automatically creating draft replies to customer inquiries
• Assigning and triaging inbound messages based on metadata
• Exporting analytics data to third-party BI tools
• Creating application channels programmatically

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Buildability
The availability of documented REST API endpoints and an official MCP implementation makes integration ready for development.

An MCP connection links Gladly AI to an external system so it can look up information or take action during a Customer Conversation . MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI systems discover and call the tools an external system offers. With an MCP connection, Gladly AI can check an order status, search a product catalog, or look up store hours while it helps a customer, using live data from your own systems. Instead of building a custom App Platform integration for every external system, you register an MCP server once. Gladly discovers the tools on that server automatically. How MCP connections work When a customer asks a question, Gladly AI decides whether one of your MCP tools can help. If it can, Gladly AI calls

Gorgias is an e-commerce helpdesk platform that provides a REST API for programmatic access to helpdesk data and a first-party Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to facilitate integration with AI assistants.

Access requirements

Unresolved

Example operations

• Search and read support tickets
• Create or update customer profiles
• List and manage account settings
• Retrieve support metrics and statistics
• Manage ticket tags and macros

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

Description
Gorgias is an e-commerce helpdesk platform that centralizes customer support conversations.

What is Gorgias MCP? The Gorgias MCP server is a Model Context Protocol server that connects Gorgias to AI agents and assistants as a set of tools. With it connected, an agent can work with Gorgias (e-commerce helpdesk — tickets, customer support and conversations) directly — instead of you copying data in and out by hand. It is a remote MCP server that uses OAuth, so you point your client at the server URL, authorize once, and the Gorgias tools become available to the model. Connect the Gorgias MCP server Connect Gorgias MCP to Claude Code 1 Add the server Use `claude mcp add` with the Gorgias MCP server URL (or its `npx` command), following the official docs. 2 Authorize Complete authentication (OAuth) so Claude Code can call the server.

Harvest
Productivity and Project Management
Research & evidence

Harvest is a time tracking and project management application that provides a REST API for programmatic interaction with account data, including time tracking, expenses, and project management.

Access requirements

Harvest offers a free plan and three paid tiers (Teams, Enterprise, and Enterprise Plus), with additional usage-based fees for exceeding limits on projects, tasks, invoices, or clients.

Example operations

• Track time entries
• Log expenses
• Create and manage projects
• Manage tasks
• Retrieve user information

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

Description
Harvest provides a REST API for interacting with account data such as time tracking, expenses, and projects.

Welcome to the Harvest API v2 Help Center Harvest API V2 Documentation Introduction Overview This is the current API V2 documentation. You can still view the legacy API V1 documentation . Help Topics Overview The Harvest V2 API is a REST API that allows you to interact with your Harvest account programmatically. You can track time, log expenses, create projects, and more. API requests Harvest requires applications to authenticate all requests with OAuth2 or Personal Access Tokens . The following HTTP methods are supported: GET POST PATCH DELETE When issuing a GET request, parameters should be included in the URL query string: curl https://api.harvestapp.com/v2/tasks?page=2&per_page=10 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \ -H

Access Types
Harvest operates on a paid subscription model with multiple tiers and usage-based fees.

Harvest pricing plans show a per-seat rate, but that’s only the base. On top of it, Harvest started charging usage-based fees once your account passes a set number of projects, tasks, invoices, or clients. This guide breaks down how Harvest app pricing works and how it compares to Clockify’s transparent, predictable pricing. Harvest has a Free plan and 3 paid tiers: Teams (from $9/seat/month annual), Enterprise (from $14/seat/month annual), and Enterprise Plus (custom). Harvest’s per-seat price is a base rate; it also has usage fees (Unlimited and Flex packages) for invoices, projects, clients, tasks, and invoiced amount after you exceed the limit. Harvest doesn’t publish its usage fee rates. Users don’t know their real bill until they

Help Scout
Support and Helpdesk
Research & evidence

Help Scout is a customer support platform that provides RESTful APIs for managing conversations, customers, and support operations, as well as a separate Docs API for knowledge base management.

Access requirements

API access requires an active Help Scout account and specific user permissions (e.g., 'Access API' permission). Some endpoints, such as reporting, are restricted to specific pricing plans like Plus and Pro.

Example operations

• List conversations with advanced filtering
• Create a new conversation
• Update conversation tags
• Retrieve Docs article details
• Delete a conversation

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

Description
Help Scout offers a primary Inbox API for managing conversations and a separate Docs API for knowledge base management.

Note: If you don't see an API key in your profile, that's because you haven't been granted the "Docs: Create new, edit settings & Collections" permission by the Account Owner or an Administrator. Auth Methods
The Inbox API uses OAuth 2.0 with Authorization Code and Client Credentials flows.

This is an HTTPS-only API and it uses OAuth 2.0 authorization , implementing Authorization Code and Client Credential flows. All requests have to be authenticated via the Authorization header: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer f4f4994a875f461ca4d4708b9e027df4" \ https://api.helpscout.net/v2/users/me The Authorization Code flow is typically used for integrations to be used by other Help Scout users. The Client Credentials flow is meant for internal integrations. All credentials must be associated with an active, invited user in the Help Scout account; a 401 error will be returned if a user does not meet these credentials. Intercom is a customer service and support platform that provides a REST API for managing resources such as contacts, companies, conversations, and tickets, as well as a specialized Fin Agent API for AI-driven support automation.

Access requirements

API access is available for developers via developer workspaces, which are free for development purposes. Production access is tied to Intercom workspace subscriptions, though specific API-only pricing tiers are not explicitly detailed in the provided documentation.

Example operations

• Create or update a company
• Create or update a contact
• Reply to, mark as read, or close conversations
• List and search resources using cursor-based pagination
• Manage tickets and ticket attributes

Auth Methods
Intercom supports OAuth 2.0 for public integrations and Bearer token authentication for private apps.

Authentication Copy To access the Intercom API, you have two authentication options depending on whether you app is public or private. An Access Token is for if you're using the API to access data in your own Intercom workspace, in other words, building a private app. OAuth is for if you're building a public app that accesses other people's Intercom data. Access Tokens Access Tokens can be used for the following cases: You want to use the API to build a private Intercom app You want to run scripts to create or get data from your Intercom workspace You want to use the API to programmatically automate certain actions in your Intercom workspace In all of these cases, the data you are accessing is your own team's customer data. Never ask users for their Access Token Asking your users for their Access Tokens rather than implementing OAuth is against our terms of service and may result in your API access being revoked. How to use the token Once you have a token, whether an access token or a token via the OAuth process, simply provide it as an Authorization:Bearer header in your requests, as shown below. If you want to go deeper on how the Authorization:Bearer header works please check out the full spec here . $ curl \ -s https://api.intercom.io/users/5321a20f72cdbb4192000013 \ -H 'Authorization:Bearer <access_token>' \ -H 'Accept:application/json' Alternatively, helper functions are provided in some of our SDKs to authorize

Api Types
The Intercom platform provides a REST API that uses JSON for data exchange.

About our REST API Copy Our REST API is a core building block of the Intercom Platform. You can use it to retrieve and update information from your own Intercom account, or to integrate Intercom into your own product. It's completely up to you and your custom use case. Regional Hosting Intercom workspaces can be hosted in three distinct regions - US, EU and Australia. If you call api.intercom.io , we'll attempt to route your request to the correct region, but if you would prefer to specify the region where you expect the data to be stored, you can do so using the endpoints below. These replace the start of the URIs for each REST API endpoint, to connect to the specific regions. For example, to call the /me endpoint for a workspace stored

in the EU, you would call https://api.eu.intercom.io/me instead of https://api.intercom.io/me . Regional Hosting Location REST Endpoint to use US https://api.intercom.io/ Europe https://api.eu.intercom.io Australia https://api.au.intercom.io Common Approaches The API uses common approaches for the following: Function Description Data API data is JSON encoded with UTF-8. API JSON is either a single object or a list of objects. Errors 4xx and 5xx responses returning JSON with error codes. Rate Limiting Controls how many requests can be made in a time window. HTTP Methods are used in accordance with HTTP (GET POST and DELETE are the primary methods used) and resources are identified using URIs. All API requests are sent over HTTPS.

Example Operations
Developers can create or update companies using the POST /companies endpoint.

Create or Update a company Copy Request You can create or update a company. Companies will be only visible in Intercom when there is at least one associated user. Companies are looked up via company_id in a POST request, if not found via company_id , the new company will be created, if found, that company will be updated. You must send either company_id or id . A request with neither returns a 400 error. Every custom attribute you send must already exist in your workspace. Sending one that doesn't returns a 400 error. Using `company_id` You can set a unique company_id value when creating a company. However, it is not possible to update company_id . Be sure to set a unique value once upon creation of the company. link anywhere on your site to open an article in the Messenger: <a href="#" onclick="Intercom('showArticle', 123)">Open article</a> Contacts Should I use the /users or /contacts endpoint? Use /contacts . In the current API, users and leads are both contacts, and you create or update them with the Create a contact ( POST /contacts ) and Update a contact ( PUT /contacts/{id} ) endpoints. POST /users is a legacy 1.x endpoint and won't work with current API versions. How do I create a contact without an email address? A contact needs at least an email or an external_id . To create a user without an email, send your own unique identifier for them as external_id . In the /contacts endpoints this field is called external_id , not user_id .

OAuth Scopes & Permissions The Fin Agent API access token is created with minimal OAuth scopes following the principle of least privilege for enhanced security. Default Scope Your Fin Agent API token has the following OAuth scopes: write_conversations - Allows replying to, marking as read, and closing conversations read_write_users - Allows creating and updating the users Fin acts on behalf of These scopes are sufficient for all Fin Agent API operations. Token Security Server-to-Server API Only Your API key must be used for server-to-server communication only. It must: Only be used in backend/server-side code Never be exposed in client-side code

Finance and Fintech
Research & evidence

iPayX is a FINTRAC-registered FX forensic audit tool that provides an API and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to analyze currency transactions, detect hidden bank spreads, and compare applied exchange rates against mid-market benchmarks.

Access requirements

iPayX offers a free tier with limited audits (3 lifetime audits, 10 audits/day for MCP) and a paid subscription tier ($199) for unlimited audits, priority routing, and full forensic reporting.

Example operations

• Run a forensic audit on a single transaction
• Fetch live mid-market currency rates
• Audit a batch of parsed transactions
• Subscribe to audit completion webhooks
• Retrieve full forensic FX reports

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Auth Methods
Jira supports basic authentication using email and API tokens.

fred@example.com:freds_api_token \ -X GET \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/2/issue/createmeta Supply basic auth headers You can construct and send basic auth headers. To do this you perform the following steps: Generate an API token for Jira using your Atlassian Account . Build a string of the form useremail:api_token . BASE64 encode the string. Linux/Unix/MacOS: 1 2 echo -n "user@example.com:api_token_string" | base64 Windows 7 and later, using Microsoft Powershell: 1 2 3 4 5 $Text = ‘user@example.com:api_token_string’ $Bytes = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($Text) $EncodedText = [Convert]::ToBase64String($Bytes) $EncodedText Supply an Authorization header with content

Developer Documentation Resources News and Updates Get Support Sign in Developer Get Support Sign in DOCUMENTATION Cloud Data Center Resources News and Updates Get support Sign in Developer Sign in DOCUMENTATION Cloud Data Center Resources News and Updates Get support Sign in Introduction Overview Authentication Authorization Rate Limiting Examples Schema changes Explorer Launch the explorer Confluence Cloud ARI Graph Store Compass Teams Cloud admin Search platform Overview of the Atlassian platform GraphQL API The Atlassian platform GraphQL API allows you to access to all sorts of Atlassian data. For example, you can use the GraphQL API to access Jira projects, Bitbucket repositories, Opsgenie teams, or cross-product work activities. The

GraphQL API
https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/atlassian-graphql-api/graphql/

Atlassian platform GraphQL API makes this data accessible using one common mechanism using the Atlassian GraphQL Gateway. About GraphQL GraphQL is a query language for APIs. This style of API allows access to linked data, which you can think of as a graph of entities . For example, you can request the work activity of a team of people and get the details for those people in the same request. With other types of APIs, such as REST APIs, this would require many requests, making GraphQL more efficient and flexible to use. Because you must specify the data attributes you want back (called fields ), the payloads can be smaller and hence faster over the network. In other words, you only get the data that you specified and no more. GraphQL APIs

Description

You will learn After reading this article, you will be able to distinguish which methods of authentication you should use for making calls with Klaviyo's server- and client-side APIs. You will also learn how to set custom scopes to protect you and your customers’ data. Server-side vs client-side APIs Check out our video on client- and server-side tracking with Klaviyo's APIs . A majority of Klaviyo’s APIs are server-side endpoints, which should be securely handled on your server rather than exposed in the browser. Handle sensitive information via server-side APIs, like bulk-creating events for one or more profiles. Client-side APIs are used to track and send user behavior data from the client to Klaviyo. They are designed to be called from

Auth Methods
Klaviyo supports private API key authentication for server-side endpoints.

publicly-searchable, client-side environments only (see Client API reference ). Klaviyo provides 3 methods of authentication including private key authentication and OAuth (used to call server-side APIs) and public key authentication (used to call client-side APIs). Read the table below to learn more about how each method can be used for authenticating API calls: Server-side APIs Client-side APIs Private key authentication All /api endpoints use API private keys to authenticate requests. If you do not use an API key for your requests, or if you use a key from the wrong account, your call will return an error. A 401 error indicates an invalid or missing API key. OAuth If you are a tech partner integrating with Klaviyo, we recommend using

Authenticate API requests | Klaviyo Developers

private API key after it’s been created. If you need to remove access to a key based on its current scope, delete it and then create a new key with the correct scope. When you have finished setting your key’s scopes, select Create . To protect your account from unauthorized access, you cannot view your private API keys in Klaviyo. After you have created your private API key, copy it to a secure location. Private keys will have the prefix pk_ followed by a longer alphanumeric string. Use a private key Private key authentication for /api endpoints is performed by setting the following request header: Authorization: Klaviyo-API-Key your-private-api-key curl curl --request GET \ --url https://a.klaviyo.com/api/{endpoint}/ \ --header

OAuth to make authorized API calls . OAuth offers multiple benefits over a private key integration, including security, usability, improved rate limits, and the ability to be listed in Klaviyo's App Marketplace. Public key authentication All /client endpoints use a public API key: your 6-character company ID, also known as a site ID. We recommend using the Klaviyo object or our Mobile SDKs for interacting with our client-side APIs. To manage API keys, you must have an Owner, Admin, or Manager role on your Klaviyo account. Private key authentication Private API keys can be used to read and write data to your Klaviyo account. Klaviyo allows you to generate multiple private keys for your applications. Research & evidence

Lark is a communication and collaboration platform that provides a comprehensive Open Platform for developers to integrate with its services, including messaging, contacts, documents, and calendar, via server-side and client-side APIs.

Access requirements

Lark APIs are categorized into Unlimited (free), Basic (metered based on Lark plan), and Advanced (usage-based, requires dedicated quota package).

Example operations

• Create a user in Contacts
• Obtain single user's information
• Modify user information
• List records in a Bitable
• Update a block in a document

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

Description
Lark provides an Open Platform for developers to access and modify data across various business domains including messaging, contacts, and documents.

Server-side APIs can help you access and modify data in the Lark system. For how to call server-side APIs, please read: How to call server-side APIs Unlimited: Core features including Authentication and Authorization, Event Subscription, and Contacts are free to use, regardless of your Lark plan. Basic: This covers most Lark features. Usage is tallied, and heavy users may need to consider a higher-tier Lark plan to avoid restrictions. Advanced: Pricing for these APIs is usage-based. To access them, you'll need to buy a dedicated quota package. For all the details, read Policy Update: Adjusting API Call Limits for Custom Apps . token When your app calls an API, it needs to contain an access token in the request Header and use the syntax Authorization:Bearer <access token> . Different APIs can support one or more types of access tokens. Using API Explorer, you can obtain the authentication credentials required by the interface automatically without additionally calling the "Get Tenant/User Access Credentials" interface. The obtained token will then be automatically filled in the interface request parameters. Access token is valid for 7200s, you need to refresh if expired Run Fill in query parameters You can fill in the request header, request body, and query parameters, modify the default values of each input parameter to initiate a call, and explore the API

Authorization Code . Please note that the authorization code is valid for 5 minutes and can only be used once. During user authorization, the user must have access to the application . For instructions on how to refresh the user_access_token , see Refresh user_access_token . If you need to obtain user information, see Get User Information . This API implementation adheres to RFC 6749 - The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework . You can integrate using standard OAuth client libraries ( recommended ). Linear
Productivity and Project Management
Research & evidence

Linear is a project management and issue tracking platform designed for software engineering teams, featuring a GraphQL-based API for data operations and native support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

Access requirements

Linear provides API access across all service levels, including the Free plan, with no separate premium integration fees. Paid plans (Basic, Business, Enterprise) are billed per-user, per-month, with annual commitments required for Basic and Business tiers.

Example operations

• Query workspace data including issues, projects, and cycles
• Create, update, or delete issues and comments
• Manage project updates and health status
• Retrieve user context and team information
• Upload files to issues

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

Description
Linear is a developer-focused issue tracking and project management platform.

Linear Linear provides fast, developer-focused issue tracking and project management software for modern software engineering teams. Track Company Project Management Version Control Dev Tools & IDEs linear.app Linear Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs & Hidden Fees Author KK Kavishka Karunanayake Last updated March 30, 2026 On this page Linear 's pricing follows a straightforward per-user model with four tiers: Free, Basic ($10/user/month), Business ($16/user/month), and Enterprise (custom pricing). Linear maintains an official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.

MCP server The Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides a standardized interface that allows any compatible AI model or agent to access your Linear data in a simple and secure way. Connect to our MCP server natively in Claude, Cursor, and other clients or use the mcp-remote module for backwards compatibility with clients that do not support remote MCP. Linear’s MCP server follows the authenticated remote MCP spec , so the server is centrally hosted and managed. The Linear MCP server has tools available for finding, creating, and updating objects in Linear like issues, projects, and comments — with more functionality on the way, and feedback on its functionality is welcomed. Auth Methods
The LinkedIn API uses OAuth 2.0 for authentication and authorization.

Flow Configure your application in the Developer Portal to obtain Client ID and Client Secret . Your application directs the browser to LinkedIn's OAuth 2.0 authorization page where the member authenticates. After authentication, LinkedIn's authorization server passes an authorization code to your application. Your application sends this code to LinkedIn and LinkedIn returns an access token. Your application uses this token to make API calls on behalf of the member. Authorization : The process of determining whether a user or app has permission to access a particular API, often through a token-based protocol such as OAuth 2.0. Note To supplement authentication and authorization, you should also secure access to APIs using TLS to protect the credentials or tokens you use for authentication or authorization. OAuth 2.0 concepts OAuth 2.0 is a standard authorization framework that's widely used to secure access to resources such as web APIs. OAuth 2.0 restricts actions of what a client app can perform on resources on behalf of the user, without ever sharing the user's credentials.

Magento
Ecommerce
Research & evidence

Magento (Adobe Commerce) is an e-commerce platform providing REST, SOAP, and GraphQL APIs for managing store operations, including customer data, orders, and product catalogs.

Access requirements

Access is determined by the edition (Open Source is free, Adobe Commerce is paid) and requires configuring API user roles and permissions within the Magento Admin panel.

Example operations

• Retrieve customer data
• Sync order information
• Manage product catalogs
• Create CMS pages
• Manage company roles and permissions

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Magento offers REST, SOAP, and GraphQL APIs for managing e-commerce features.

Mailchimp
Marketing, Ads, Email and Social
Research & evidence

Mailchimp Marketing API is a REST-based interface that allows developers to programmatically interact with Mailchimp account data, including campaigns, audiences, reports, and e-commerce resources.

Access requirements

API access is available to Mailchimp users; paid users have access to email and chat support for troubleshooting. API keys are generated within the user account and are subject to expiration policies.

Example operations

• List and manage marketing campaigns
• Manage audience lists and list members
• Retrieve campaign reports and click details
• Manage e-commerce store customers
• Start or pause automation workflows

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

Description
The Mailchimp Marketing API is a REST-based service for managing marketing resources like campaigns and subscribers.

Skip to navigation This page is for Mailchimp Marketing API. The Marketing API generally follows REST conventions, with some deviations. Resources are typically nouns like subscribers or campaigns . Subresources can be multiply nested under resources. Actions are usually represented by HTTP methods . Actions that do not correspond to HTTP methods are collected under an actions/ subresource. Responses use the generic JSON content type. We use the OpenAPI Specification (formerly known as Swagger) to describe each endpoint. The API self-description also contains type information to help you error-check your requests. The root url for the API is https://api.mailchimp.com/3.0/ . All API endpoints for your account are available relative to this

https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/api-concepts/api-structure
Auth Methods
Mailchimp supports API key authentication and OAuth 2.0 for third-party integrations.

Skip to navigation On this page Choose a credential Authenticate with an API key or OAuth 2 token User access and revocation Scroll to top This page is for Mailchimp Marketing API. Every request to the Marketing API carries a credential. There are two kinds, and which one you need depends on whose account data you’re reaching for. Choose a credential An API key authenticates against the account that created it. Use one when your code couples your application’s data to your own Mailchimp account. It requires no server to handle a redirect, so it’s the fastest way to make a first request. OAuth 2 authenticates against an account belonging to someone else. Any integration a third party installs needs it. You can start development against your

If that user is removed from the account, the token is revoked. Access is also bounded by the user level (role) of that user, and a role can change over time. monday.com is a work operating system that provides a GraphQL-based platform API for managing workflows, boards, items, and account data.

Access requirements

API access is available on all plans, including the free tier, with rate limits based on complexity and daily call volume.

Example operations

• Query board items by ID
• Create a new item on a board
• List users in an account
• Subscribe to board-level events via webhooks
• Update column values for an item

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

Description
monday.com is a work OS that allows teams to manage workflows and provides an application layer for reading and updating data.

Stop! Before you scroll... Get your answer faster. Ask our AI assistant any question about the monday API and get an instant answer. → Welcome to monday.com, a work OS where teams create and shape their own workflows in minutes, code-free. Our mission is to help teams outdo their best, fulfilling their potential, and collaborating more effectively. The monday GraphQL API is part of the monday apps framework . It is an application layer that allows apps to read and update data inside a monday.com account. It supports operations boards, items, column values, users, workspaces, and more. Why use the API? On this page Summary API quick reference Authentication User object / data model Core endpoints Rate limits, pagination, and events SCIM API status Common scenarios Why building this yourself is a trap Summary and recommendation Monday.com's API is a single GraphQL endpoint (`POST https://api.monday.com/v2`) - there are no REST-style resource URLs. Authentication uses either a personal API token (no `Bearer` prefix in the Authorization header) or an OAuth 2.0 access token (`Bearer` prefix required). Personal tokens do not expire; OAuth tokens do and require refresh handling. User operations require `users:read` and `users:write` scopes at minimum. Example Operations
Developers can query items by ID, create new items, list users, and update column values.

Items are core objects in the monday.com platform that hold the actual data within the board. To better illustrate the platform, imagine each board as a table, and an item is a single row in that table. Take one row, fill it with whatever information you'd like, and you now have an item ! 🚧 Want to read all items on a board? The items object allows you to query specific items by their IDs. If you want to read all items on a board, use the items_page object instead! Queries Get items Required scope: boards:read Returns an array containing metadata about one or a collection of specific items Can only be queried directly at the root; can't be nested within another query GraphQL query { items(ids: [1234567890, 9876543210, 2345678901]) {

Item data is stored in columns that hold particular information based on the column type. Each type expects a different set of parameters to update its values. When sending data to a particular column, use a JSON-formatted string. If you're using JavaScript, you can use JSON.stringify() to convert a JSON object into a string. You can also use simple values in this mutation or combine them with regular values. Read more about sending data for each column in our column types reference . endpoints List Users Method: POST URL: https://api.monday.com/v2 Watch out for: Uses page-based pagination (page + limit), not cursor. Max limit is 500 per page. Request example { "query": "{ users(limit: 50, page: 1) { id name email is_admin is_guest enabled } }" } Response example { "data": { "users": [ { "id": "12345", "name": "Jane Doe", "email": "jane@example.com", "is_admin": false, "is_guest": false, "enabled": true } ] } } Get User by ID Method: POST URL: https://api.monday.com/v2 Watch out for: ids parameter accepts an array; returns empty array if user not found rather than an error. Request example { "query": "{ users(ids: [12345]) { id name email title phone time_zone_identifier teams { id name } } }" }

Developer, Infra and Data platforms
Research & evidence

MongoDB Atlas Administration API is a RESTful interface that enables programmatic management of Atlas infrastructure, including clusters, database users, and network access settings.

Access requirements

Access to the Administration API is subject to Atlas billing; users must have a valid credit card on file to avoid account locking if charges are incurred.

Example operations

• Create and manage MongoDB Atlas clusters
• Configure network access lists for projects
• Create and manage database users
• List Atlas projects and clusters
• Retrieve cluster connection strings

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

Description
The Atlas Administration API uses a REST architectural style to provide programmatic access to administrative features in MongoDB Atlas.

Atlas Administration API Reference Copy page The Atlas Administration API follows the principles of the REST architectural style to expose a number of internal resources that enable programmatic access to administrative features in Atlas . To view the full list of available Atlas Administration API endpoints, see the Atlas Administration API Specification. The Atlas Administration API doesn't provide access to the data stored in your clusters. To read or write data in a database, you must authenticate to your cluster using the credentials for a database user with the appropriate read or write roles . You can use the Atlas Administration API to create and manage database users. As with changes made through the Atlas web interface, changes

MongoDB Atlas Administration API 2.0 Ask AI View as Markdown Copy as Markdown https://cloud.mongodb.com The MongoDB Atlas Administration API allows developers to manage all components in MongoDB Atlas. The Atlas Administration API supports OAuth2 Service Accounts and HTTP Digest-based API keys. Service accounts are the recommended authentication method and API keys are considered a legacy option. To authenticate with a Service Account, first exchange its client ID and secret for an access token using the OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials flow. Atlas provides a token endpoint at POST https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/oauth/token , which returns a Bearer token that is reusable and valid for 1 hour (3600 seconds). Research & evidence

MrScraper is a web scraping and data extraction platform that provides AI-powered scraping agents, workflow automation, and web search capabilities accessible via a REST API, CLI, and SDKs.

Access requirements

Access requires an API token generated from the user dashboard; specific pricing tiers are not detailed in the provided documentation, though enterprise-only proxy pricing is mentioned.

Example operations

• Run a web search query to retrieve ranked results
• Execute a pre-configured AI scraper workflow via API
• Retrieve page content as HTML or Markdown
• Verify account status and token usage
• Self-heal or repair a scraper workflow programmatically

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

MrScraper is a platform for web scraping and data extraction that offers AI-driven agents and workflow automation.

Neo4j has the following authentication (auth) providers that can perform user and role authentication: Native auth provider Neo4j provides a native auth provider that stores user and role information in the system database. The following parameters control this provider: dbms.security.auth_enabled (Default: true ) — Enable auth requirement to access Neo4j. Returns the raw key once; also stored encrypted-at-rest so it can be revealed later. List GET /v1/auth/api-keys Reveal GET /v1/auth/api-keys/{id}/reveal — owner-only (non-owners get 404 ; revoked or pre-encryption keys get 410 ). Rotate POST /v1/auth/api-keys/{id}/rotate — mints a new key and revokes the old one. Revoke DELETE /v1/auth/api-keys/{id} — added to a blocklist for 30 days; effective on the next request. Netlify
Developer, Infra and Data platforms
Research & evidence

Netlify is a developer platform that provides a REST API and CLI for managing web projects, including atomic site deploys, form submissions, DNS configuration, and build management.

Access requirements

Netlify offers a free tier with generous limits, while Pro and Business plans are available for higher scale and advanced features. API usage is subject to rate limits, typically 500 requests per minute for most operations.

Example operations

• Manage atomic deploys of sites and apps
• Manage form submissions
• Inject JavaScript snippets
• Manage DNS settings
• Trigger builds and manage site configuration

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Overview The Model Context Protocol is an emerging standard protocol for connecting code agents with MCP servers, allowing them to manage resources and perform tasks using natural language. The Netlify MCP Server acts as a bridge, providing API access, CLI tools, prompts, and more for your agents. Mcp Status
Netlify maintains an official MCP server.

MCP Server Netlify MCP Server follows the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to enable code agents to use the Netlify API and CLI—so they can create new projects, build, deploy, and manage your Netlify resources using natural language prompts. Overview The Model Context Protocol is an emerging standard protocol for connecting code agents with MCP servers, allowing them to manage resources and perform tasks using natural language. The Netlify MCP Server acts as a bridge, providing API access, CLI tools, prompts, and more for your agents. You can connect to the Netlify MCP Server using a variety of MCP clients, including: Windsurf Cursor Claude Copilot (VSCode) Cline Warp LM Studio See the full list Use Cases With Netlify MCP Server, your AI

Notion
Productivity and Project Management
Research & evidence

Notion is a productivity and project management application that provides a REST API for interacting with workspaces, including managing pages, databases, and blocks.

Access requirements

The Notion API enforces rate limits based on the workspace plan, with Business and Enterprise plans allowing 600 requests per minute and other plans allowing 180 requests per minute. Per-connection limits for data source queries are approximately 3 requests per second.

Example operations

• Create a new page with markdown content
• Search for pages or databases in a workspace
• Query and retrieve database entries
• Read page content as Markdown
• Update page content or database views

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

Description
Notion provides a developer API to interact with workspaces, supporting pages, databases, and blocks.

On this page Notion is a novel note-taking application. Users can create pages that support third-party integrations and interactive elements as well as databases with different views. They recently released the beta version of their developer API which can be used to interact with your Notion workspace from code. Structure In order to understand the API, first, one has to understand how the content in Notion is organized: The basic building blocks are pages and databases. Both can have multiple pages and databases as children. Pages can also contain so-called “blocks”, which can be of different types and contain the actual content (pages are blocks, too - but more on that later). Auth Methods
Notion supports OAuth 2.0 for public and internal integrations.

What is authorization? Authorization is the process of granting a connection or token access to Notion data. Internal connections use a static credential called an internal connection API token, personal access tokens use a user-scoped static token, and OAuth integrations and public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol. Internal connection auth flow set-up To use an internal connection, start by creating your connection in the Developer portal . The internal connection will be associated with the workspace of your choice. You are required to be a workspace owner to create a connection. Create a new connection from the Developer portal. Once the connection is created, you can update its settings as needed under the Configuration tab and

Notion API authorization
https://developers.notion.com/guides/authorization/overview
Auth Methods
Notion supports personal access tokens (PATs) using bearer token authentication.

access token authentication Personal access tokens (PATs) are created directly by a Notion user in the Developer portal . There is no OAuth flow and no page picker. A PAT acts as the user who created it and uses that user’s permissions in the selected workspace. Use a PAT when a script, CLI workflow, Worker, or trusted tool should act as you. Use an internal connection for team-owned workspace automations, or an OAuth integration when each user needs to authorize your app. PATs use the same Authorization header as other credentials for the Notion API: HTTP GET /v1/users/me HTTP / 1.1 Authorization : Bearer {PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN} Notion-Version : 2026-03-11 See Personal access tokens for creation steps, workspace admin controls, tier

Notion API authorization
https://developers.notion.com/guides/authorization/overview
Auth Methods
Internal connections use a static API token for authentication.

What is an internal connection? An internal connection is scoped to a single Notion workspace. Only members of that workspace can use it. Internal connections are ideal for team-owned automations and workflows — things like syncing data from external tools, sending notifications when pages change, or powering internal dashboards. Internal connections use a static credential called an internal connection API token. There’s no OAuth flow to implement — you get a token immediately when you create the connection, and you use that same token for every API request. If you want a token that acts as your own Notion user for a script, CLI workflow, Worker, or trusted tool, use a personal access token instead. PATs use the creator’s page permissions
