endpoint is described in more detail in the API reference docs for creating a token . The request is authorized using HTTP Basic Authentication. The credential is a colon-delimited combination of the connection’s CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET , like so: CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET Find both of these values in the Developer portal . Note that in HTTP Basic Authentication , credentials are base64 encoded before being added to the Authorization header. Access Types
Notion API access is available across different workspace plans, with rate limits scaling based on the plan.

Workspace plan limits are separate from request limits. See Workspace block limits for the Free workspace limit that takes effect on September 8, 2026. Rate limits The Notion API enforces two rate limits: a per-connection limit and a per-workspace limit. Some endpoints also have their own limit. Per-connection limit Each connection has a fixed budget of requests per 60-second window, based on the workspace’s plan: Workspace plan Limit Business and Enterprise 600 requests per minute (an average of 10 per second) All other plans 180 requests per minute (an average of 3 per second) The budget can be spent at any pace within the window — spread out evenly or in a single burst. here (not sure why the authentication part is missing), but there are still some gotchas I wanna point out. The whole API is versioned and requires the user to provide the targeted version number in the header: “Notion-Version”: “2021–08–16” . To list all pages in the users’ workspace, you can use the /v1/search route without an actual query. The pagination implementation is horrible: For example, they won’t tell you how many entries (or pagination pages) your query results in. You only get a cursor, which you can use to request the next couple of results after your last request. Each page is also a block. You can just use the page id in the block API. To get all blocks of a page, you send a GET request to /v1/blocks/*<page*_id>/children

significantly more token-efficient for AI agents: retrieve-page-markdown — Read a page's full content as Markdown ( GET /v1/pages/{page_id}/markdown ). Pass include_transcript: true to inline meeting-note transcripts. update-page-markdown — Edit a page's content with Markdown ( PATCH /v1/pages/{page_id}/markdown ). Prefer replace_content to overwrite the whole page, or update_content for targeted find-and-replace edits. These endpoints require Notion API version 2026-03-11 . The server now sources the Notion-Version header per operation from the OpenAPI spec, so these tools use 2026-03-11 while the rest of the API continues to use 2025-09-03 — no configuration needed. Example Operations
The API supports creating and updating database views.

Shows workspace members and guests with their IDs, names, emails (if available), and types (person or bot). Supports cursor-based pagination to iterate through all users in the workspace. notion-create-view Create a new view on a Notion database. Use "fetch" first to get the database_id and data_source_id (from tags in the response). Supported types: table, board, list, calendar, timeline, gallery, form, chart, map, dashboard. notion-update-view Update a view's name, filters, sorts, or display configuration. Use "fetch" to get view IDs from database responses. Only include fields you want to change. The "configure" param uses the same DSL as create_view. Marketing, Ads, Email and Social
Research & evidence

The Pinterest API (v5) is a RESTful platform enabling developers to manage Pins, boards, ad campaigns, and product catalogs, and to retrieve analytics for creators and advertisers.

Access requirements

Developers must register an app and undergo a review process to obtain Trial access. Standard access is required for full production functionality and higher rate limits.

Example operations

• Create and manage Pins and boards
• Retrieve Pin and ad analytics
• Manage ad accounts and campaigns
• Manage product catalogs and feeds
• Follow users and retrieve account information

Integration assessment

Integration is feasible subject to documented requirements. Requirements or restrictions: Requires application review and approval by Pinterest; Standard access requires a video demonstration of the OAuth flow

• Requires application review and approval by Pinterest
• Standard access requires a video demonstration of the OAuth flow

Auth Methods
Pinterest API services require OAuth 2.0 authentication, utilizing Authorization Code or Client Credentials grant types.

access token . Our implementation of grant types and access tokens follows OAuth 2.0 specifications. To learn more about OAuth and grant types, see the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework RFC . Authorization Code grant What this type is for: This grant type is designed for web apps that access a user's data on behalf of that user. It is the only grant type that gives you access to the full range of capabilities offered by the Pinterest API. It requires user authentication. Authorization Code is the most secure grant type because: The user must explicitly approve the scopes requested by your app. The user's credentials are never shared with the client (your app) directly. The access token is sent directly to the client server, not the user's

Research & evidence

Pipedrive is a CRM and sales platform that provides a RESTful API for integrating external software, automating sales processes, and managing CRM data.

Access requirements

API access is included with every Pipedrive plan, though administrators can restrict individual user access to their own API tokens via permission sets.

Example operations

• Retrieve and manage deals, persons, and organizations
• Create new leads based on external data
• Assign tasks to sales teams
• Pull call lists and customer information
• Manage webhooks for real-time data updates

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Glossary A glossary of Plaid terminology Tokens, identifiers, and keys Plaid tokens are in the format [type]-[environment]-[uuid] , where the type may be public , access , link , assets , processor , or user , and the environment may be sandbox or production ; a token will only ever be valid within the environment it was created. The UUID is a 32 character hexadecimal string in the pattern of 8-4-4-4-12 characters and conforms to the RFC 4122 standard . Access token An access_token is a token that can be used to make API requests related to a specific Item. You will typically obtain an access_token by calling /item/public_token/exchange . For more details, see the Token exchange flow . An access_token does not expire, although it may

Processor token A processor_token is a token used by a Plaid partner to make API calls on your behalf. You can obtain a processor_token by calling /processor/token/create or /processor/stripe/bank_account_token/create and providing an access_token . The processor_token does not expire. Once successfully passed to the processor, it can be either deleted from your database, or retained to manage the processor's permissions and access via /processor/token/permissions/set . Dashboard MCP server Connect an LLM application to Plaid Dashboard tools Plaid offers two Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers: The Dashboard MCP server is a remote MCP server hosted by Plaid. It provides Production diagnostics and analytics tools, including tools for debugging Items, reviewing Link conversion data, and checking usage metrics. The Plaid AI coding toolkit includes a local MCP server for development. It runs as a subprocess of an MCP client, such as Claude, Cursor, Codex, VS Code, or Zed, and provides tools for mock data generation, documentation search, Sandbox tokens, and webhook simulation. This article covers the Dashboard MCP server. You can connect to it from an MCP client, or you can use it in a model provider's API

You are an agent setting up Plain, a customer support platform, for the person you’re working with. You do the setup through Plain’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at https://mcp.plain.com/mcp , which signs in as that person with OAuth. Don’t ask the person for an API key: the MCP server needs none, and an API key belongs to a machine user, not to them. Steps 1 through 4 establish the connection and where to resume. Before you make any change in step 5, tell the person exactly what you propose and wait for their approval. When the person has to choose, use your host’s question tool if it has one, such as AskUserQuestion in Claude Code. Otherwise ask in chat. Auth Methods
Podio supports OAuth 2.0 authentication with multiple grant types including authorization_code, password, refresh_token, and app.

/oauth/token/v2 Gets a new access token for use when accessing the API. Podio supports 4 ways of obtaining an access token: password : Use the end users mail and password to access the API. This is only valid for trusted clients authorization_code : Use the authorization code obtained from step one of the authorization (see the area for more information) refresh_token : Use the refresh token obtained previously from one of the above methods. app : Login as an app with the id of the app and the apps login token This operation can return a wide variety of error codes. keys as a tab under your account settings. What are the limitation on API requests? To ensure Podio runs well for everyone, API integrations are subject to two base rate limits. Limit A applies to resource-intensive API operations, while Limit B applies to all other API operations. If you exceed an applicable limit, affected API requests will return errors. See the Rate Limits section for the current limits and information about monitoring your usage. Can I get a higher rate limit? Yes. If your API integration requires a higher rate limit, you can request your contract owner to purchase an API Add-on for the relevant API key. The API Add-on increases both Limit A and Limit B, with multiple tiers available to suit different usage

Make a POST like this: HTTP METHOD: POST URL: https://api.podio.com/oauth/token/v 2 HEADER: "Content-Type: application/json" BODY: { "grant_type" : "authorization_code" , "client_id" : YOUR_APP_ID , "redirect_uri" : YOUR_URL , "client_secret" : YOUR_APP_SECRET , "code" : THE_AUTHORIZATION_CODE , }

Pumble is a team communication and collaboration platform that provides an API addon for automating workflows, sending messages, and managing channels via HTTP requests.

Access requirements

The Pumble API addon is available on all Pumble plans for Owners, Admins, and Members.

• Add reactions to messages
• Create new channels
• List channels and direct messages

generate an API key within your Pumble workspace administration panel. This token must be passed inside the HTTP header of every request as a bearer token. Now, you can generate API keys directly in Pumble: In the left sidebar, click API. Select Add API key. Enter API key name. Click Generate to complete the action. Keep in mind that the rate limit is up to 1000 requests per minute per user. You can find the complete list of available actions in the Swagger documentation. Pumble helps you build a more productive and context-aware environment inside your collaboration workspace. Setting up the Pumble API addon The Pumble API addon provides simple HTTP endpoints to handle messaging actions inside your workspace . It is available on all Pumble plans to Owners, Admins, and Members . However, it doesn’t support an interactive message builder framework or an Events API. It is built to effectively handle: Generating unique workspace API keys Sending messages Deleting messages Adding reactions or emojis in active threads Creating new channels via standard POST requests This focused scope keeps the API straightforward to implement and maintain. Pumble helps you build a more productive and context-aware environment inside your collaboration workspace. Setting up the Pumble API addon The Pumble API addon provides simple HTTP endpoints to handle messaging actions inside your workspace . It is available on all Pumble plans to Owners, Admins, and Members . However, it doesn’t support an interactive message builder framework or an Events API. It is built to effectively handle: Generating unique workspace API keys Sending messages Deleting messages Adding reactions or emojis in active threads Creating new channels via standard POST requests This focused scope keeps the API straightforward to implement and maintain. The API supports searching for issues using complex filters on fields like created_at, state, and tags.

Question Answer Which field is filtered? The issue's created_at . Are the bounds inclusive? start_time is inclusive. end_time is exclusive. Are both required? Yes. Leaving either out returns 400 . Maximum window 365 days between start_time and end_time . Order Newest created_at first. Page size limit defaults to 20,000, the maximum. To filter on another timestamp, such as updated_at , resolved_at , or latest_message_activity_at , use POST /issues/search . Search has no maximum window: Search filters Every POST .../search endpoint except feature requests takes a filter object with the same structure. QuickBooks
Finance and Fintech
Research & evidence

QuickBooks Online is a cloud-based accounting platform that provides a REST API for managing financial data, including invoices, customers, and payments.

Access requirements

The Intuit App Partner Program uses a tiered model where data creation (Core API) is free and unlimited, while data retrieval (CorePlus API) is metered with a free tier and paid tiers starting at $300/month.

Example operations

• Create invoices
• Update customer records
• Query account balances
• Fetch financial reports
• Retrieve bill details

Integration assessment

Integration is feasible subject to documented requirements. Requirements or restrictions: Strict rate limits of 500 requests per minute per company; 1-hour access token expiry requiring token management; Usage-based pricing for data retrieval operations; Requirement for an Intuit Developer account and OAuth 2.0 implementation

• Strict rate limits of 500 requests per minute per company
• 1-hour access token expiry requiring token management
• Usage-based pricing for data retrieval operations
• Requirement for an Intuit Developer account and OAuth 2.0 implementation

Rate Limits Intuit's pricing tiers aren't the only constraint. The rate limits impose a hard ceiling on how fast your integration can operate, and navigating them requires non-trivial engineering investment. QuickBooks Online enforces 500 requests per minute per company (realm ID) with a maximum of 10 concurrent requests per app. Batch operations are limited to 40 requests per minute, while resource-intensive endpoints drop to 200 requests per minute. Exceeding these limits results in HTTP 429 "Too Many Requests" errors. Access requirements

API access is enabled by default in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer Edition orgs. Professional Edition orgs can add API access as an add-on. Users must have the 'API Enabled' permission in their user profile.

• run Apex unit tests

Auth Methods
SCAPI and OCAPI support OAuth 2.0 for authentication.

OCAPI OAuth 2.0 The OAuth 2.0 protocol is used for authentication and authorization where the shopping customer context provided by JWT doesn’t fit. When using the Data API in a server-to-server scenario, OAuth is used to authenticate requests in the context of a client ID, also known as a Client Credentials Grant . When using the Shop API or Data API in a scenario in which a Business Manager user interacts with the system, OAuth is used to authenticate requests in the context of the user. This topic assumes that you’re familiar with OAuth 2.0. For more information, see the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework IETF specification. you can send the key in an Authorization header or as an apikey query parameter. Generate a key from the API Dashboard in your SE Ranking or SE Visible account. Method 1: Authorization header (recommended) Send the key in an Authorization header with the value Token YOUR_API_KEY . Copy curl -X GET 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/se-visible/subscription' \ -H 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY' Method 2: Query parameter Pass the key as an apikey query parameter. Copy curl -X GET 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/se-visible/subscription?apikey=YOUR_API_KEY' Note: The apikey parameter must always be sent as a GET parameter, even when other data is sent in the request body. • Retrieve aggregate email performance statistics
• Manage marketing campaign automation workflows

be created within Sentry on the "User settings" page ( User settings > Personal Tokens ) and assigned specific scopes. Auth Methods
Sentry supports authentication via bearer tokens passed in the authorization header.

Home API Reference Authentication Copy page API Authentication Auth Tokens Authentication tokens are passed using an auth header, and are used to authenticate as a user or organization account with the API. In our documentation, we have several placeholders that appear between curly braces or chevrons, such as {API_KEY} or <auth_token> , which you will need to replace with one of your authentication tokens in order to use the API call effectively. For the string format of auth tokens, organization tokens, DSNs, and legacy API keys, see Token and Credential Formats . For example, when the documentation says: Bash Copied curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer {TOKEN}' https://sentry.io/api/0/organizations/ { organization_slug } /projects/ curl -H

the config file): SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN ( auth.token ): The authentication token to use for all communication with Sentry. Sentry provides a free tier with a monthly error quota.

Engineering time is going into tuning sample rates and quota management across five separate meters, rather than debugging. Teams report spending real time adjusting sample rates per environment and managing per-project quotas work that has nothing to do with debugging applications. You need infrastructure and log correlation alongside errors, and are running Sentry next to a second tool to get it. Sentry Pricing 2026: Full Cost Breakdown by Plan & Team Size
https://middleware.io/blog/sentry-pricing/
Access Types
Sentry offers paid plans based on usage meters for errors, transactions, and other events.

Try Middleware 14 days free trial with unlimited data ingestion and then pay as you go. Get Started Sentry bills differently than most observability platforms: instead of metering data volume, it meters events, errors, spans, replays, logs, and attachments each with its own quota and its own overage rate. Overages on the Team plan run from $0.0003625 per error in the 50k–100k tier down to $0.0001500 per error at 20M+ events, while Business tier overage rates run higher, from $0.0011125 per error down to $0.0003000 at the top tier. At low volume this is genuinely predictable. Past a certain scale, the number of separately-metered categories starts to matter; a single noisy deploy can spike one category without warning. No per-event billing.

API and any access tokens (API keys), or other sensitive information. Authentication Approaches When choosing an authentication method, it is important to consider your integration scenario. Is the integration machine-to-machine without user interaction, or do you want user consent and interaction? If your scenario involves user consent and interaction, it's typically best to use OAuth with Smartsheet. Note that the Smartsheet implementation of OAuth 2.0 is a 3-legged process, which requires human intervention. See OAuth Walkthrough for details. Snowflake provides a REST API suite that enables developers to programmatically interact with and control various resources within the Snowflake Data Cloud.

Squarespace
Ecommerce
Research & evidence

Squarespace is a website builder and ecommerce platform that provides REST-based Commerce APIs for managing store operations, including products, orders, inventory, and transactions, as well as an official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI agent integration.

Access requirements

Unresolved

Example operations

• Retrieve store pages
• View inventory stock levels
• Manage discount records
• Create, update, or delete webhook subscriptions
• View transactional order and donation data

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

Description
Squarespace offers Commerce APIs for managing storefront data and an official MCP server for AI assistant connectivity.

Overview of the Squarespace MCP Server The Squarespace MCP server connects AI assistants to Squarespace. It's built on the Model Context Protocol , an open standard for connecting AI applications to outside tools, so assistants like Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT can look things up and make changes on Squarespace in the middle of a conversation. With it, someone can describe a new business and leave the chat with a domain ready to buy, or ask "which orders still need shipping?" about their own store and get a live answer. Connect a Client → Add Squarespace to Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, or another MCP client. Access Types
Custom application development using Squarespace Commerce APIs requires the Commerce Advanced plan.

Extensions are required to use OAuth. Custom applications With Squarespace's Commerce Advanced plan, you can develop a custom application for a Squarespace merchant site. Follow the steps below to generate an API key for a custom application. Log in to a Squarespace site. In the left nav, click Settings ; scroll down and click Advanced . Click Developer API Keys . Click the GENERATE KEY button. In the dialog, add a key name under "KEY NAME", and select one or more Commerce APIs under "PERMISSIONS" and permission level. Record the generated key in a safe and secure place. For security reasons, this is the only time the API key is visible. API keys will never expire as long as the merchant site remains active. Overview of the Squarespace MCP Server The Squarespace MCP server connects AI assistants to Squarespace. It's built on the Model Context Protocol , an open standard for connecting AI applications to outside tools, so assistants like Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT can look things up and make changes on Squarespace in the middle of a conversation. With it, someone can describe a new business and leave the chat with a domain ready to buy, or ask "which orders still need shipping?" about their own store and get a live answer. Supabase
Developer, Infra and Data platforms
Research & evidence

Supabase is a developer platform that provides auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs for Postgres databases, along with authentication, authorization, and management services.

Access requirements

Supabase offers a tiered pricing model based on usage, including Monthly Active Users (MAU) quotas. Access control is managed via organization and project-scoped roles such as Owner, Administrator, Developer, and Read-Only.

Example operations

• Fetch rows from a table via REST GET
• Insert data into a table via REST POST
• Execute database functions via RPC .rpc() call
• Query data using GraphQL
• Retrieve project API credentials via Management API

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Updated Nov 24, 2026 Supabase provides granular access controls to manage permissions across your organizations and projects. For each organization and project, a member can have one of the following roles: Owner : full access to everything in organization and project resources. Administrator : full access to everything in organization and project resources except updating organization settings, transferring projects outside of the organization, and adding new owners. Developer : read-only access to organization resources, full content access to project resources but cannot change any project settings. Read-Only : read-only access to organization and project resources. No-access : no access to any organization or project resources by

Api Types
Supabase provides a GraphQL API reflected from the database schema.

The Supabase GraphQL API is automatically reflected from your database's schema using pg_graphql . It supports: Basic CRUD operations (Create/Read/Update/Delete) Support for Tables, Views, Materialized Views, and Foreign Tables Arbitrarily deep relationships among tables/views User defined computed fields Postgres' security model - including Row Level Security, Roles, and Grants All requests resolve in a single round-trip leading to fast response times and high throughput. If you haven't created a Supabase project, do that here so you can follow along with the guide. Quickstart https://<PROJECT_REF>.supabase.co/graphql/v1 is your project's GraphQL API endpoint. are ideal for multi-step transactions, business rules, or performance-sensitive operations that work across multiple tables. These functions can be exposed via the Supabase API using the .rpc() call or accessed directly through the REST endpoint at /rpc/<function-name> . Named parameters are passed as a simple JSON payload, making integration clean and declarative. standards. Let’s say you define a customers table. The acronym API stands for "Application Programming Interface", a series of instructions by which a platform offers services to other platforms. It's a strategic gateway for external developers, enabling them to access specific functionality or data from a platform in a structured, secure way. It's like a set of ready-to-use tools that make it easy to build new applications, services, or combinations. In short, systeme.io opens up to other platforms to offer its services where it has added value. 2. How does our public API work? Access tokens are app-scoped (unique to the app and user pair) and can be short-lived or long-lived. API requests that query Threads users or publish Threads media must

Twenty
CRM and Sales
Research & evidence

Twenty is an open-source CRM platform that provides schema-per-tenant APIs, allowing users to interact with both built-in and custom objects through REST and GraphQL endpoints.

Access requirements

Unresolved

Example operations

• Create, read, update, and delete records for People, Companies, and Opportunities
• Programmatically create, modify, or delete objects and fields via Metadata API
• Perform batch operations for up to 60 records per request
• Execute batch upserts using GraphQL
• Query and filter data with field selection

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

Description
Twenty is an open-source CRM that generates schema-specific APIs for both built-in and custom objects.

Schema-per-tenant APIs There is no static API reference for Twenty. Each workspace has its own schema — when you add a custom object (say Invoice ), it immediately gets REST and GraphQL endpoints identical to built-in objects like Company or Person . The API is generated from the schema, so endpoints use your object and field names directly — no opaque IDs. Your workspace-specific API documentation is available under Settings → Developers → API after creating an API key. It includes an interactive playground where you can execute real calls against your data. Two APIs Core API — /rest/ and /graphql/ CRUD on records: People, Companies, Opportunities, your custom objects. Query, filter, traverse relations. Metadata API — /rest/metadata/ and

/metadata/ Schema management: create/modify/delete objects, fields, and relations. This is how you programmatically change your data model. Both are available as REST and GraphQL. Example Operations
REST endpoints support field selection via query parameters to optimize data retrieval.

Batch operations Both REST and GraphQL support batching up to 60 records per request — create, update, or delete. GraphQL also supports batch upsert (create-or-update in one call) using plural names like CreateCompanies . Selecting fields (REST) REST record endpoints accept a fields query parameter to return only the fields you need: GET /rest/people?fields=id,name,emails,company id is always returned. Composite fields (like emails or name ) are selected as a whole by their field name. A many-to-one relation field returns its join column (e.g. companyId ) with depth=0 . One-to-many relation fields are only returned with depth=1 . With depth=1 , only the relation fields listed in fields are expanded. Unknown fields, or fields your role

Your workspace-specific API documentation is available under Settings → Developers → API after creating an API key. It includes an interactive playground where you can execute real calls against your data. Twilio supports OAuth 2.0, API Keys (Main, Standard, and Restricted), and legacy Auth Token authentication.

Twilio requires authentication on every API request. When you create a Twilio account, Twilio generates an Account SID and an Auth Token. The Auth Token provides broad account access and should be protected like a high-privilege password. Auth Methods
Vonage APIs support Basic authentication using API keys and secrets.

Bearer Production Basic Authentication Basic Authentication sends your API Key and API Secret Base64-encoded in the Authorization header. You can find these credentials in your API settings in the Vonage Dashboard. It is the simplest way to get started with Verify, since no Vonage Application setup is required, and your credentials are immediately available from the Vonage Dashboard . How It Works Copy Authorization: Basic <base64(api_key:api_secret)> Warning: API Key/Secret are sensitive! If you expose them publicly (frontend code, GitHub repos, etc.), anyone can abuse your account. Create the Request Header First, concatenate your API Key and Secret: API_KEY:API_SECRET . Then, Base64 encode the result. Learn more here . Finally, send it

Auth Methods
Vonage APIs support JWT Bearer authentication for enhanced security and feature access.

strongly recommended. JWT A JWT (JSON Web Token) is an open standard ( RFC 7519 ) for securely transmitting information between parties as a JSON object. The object can optionally be encrypted and signed with a private/public key. JWT Bearer Authentication uses a JSON Web Token signed with your Vonage Application's private key. This method unlocks the full capabilities of Verify, including event and summary callbacks, webhook configuration, and ACL-scoped tokens. How It Works Copy Authorization: Bearer <JWT> The JWT is generated using your Application ID and Private Key, both obtained when creating a Vonage Application in the Dashboard. Research & evidence

WooCommerce is an e-commerce plugin for WordPress that provides a REST API for interacting with store data such as products, orders, customers, and coupons.

Access requirements

Unresolved

Example operations

• Retrieve product lists
• Create new orders
• Update customer information
• Manage inventory stock levels
• Retrieve sales reports

Integration assessment

Documentation indicates that integration is feasible.

Supporting claims

Description
WooCommerce is a plugin for WordPress that offers programmatic APIs to interact with store data.

On this page Copy markdown Copies the current page content as markdown format to your clipboard WooCommerce provides a number of programmatic APIs to interact with WooCommerce store data. WC REST API ​ The WC REST API is a powerful part of WooCommerce which lets you read and write various parts of WooCommerce data such as orders, products, coupons, customers, and shipping zones. It based on the WordPress REST API . Explore the WC REST API documentation. Store API ​ The Store API provides public REST API endpoints for the development of customer-facing cart, checkout, and product functionality. In contrast to the WooCommerce REST API, the Store API is unauthenticated and does not provide access to sensitive store data or other customer

Auth Methods
WooCommerce supports API key authentication generated via the WordPress admin interface.

On this page Copy markdown Copies the current page content as markdown format to your clipboard WooCommerce includes two ways to authenticate with the WP REST API. It is also possible to authenticate using any WP REST API authentication plugin or method. REST API keys ​ Pre-generated keys can be used to authenticate use of the REST API endpoints. New keys can be generated either through the WordPress admin interface or they can be auto-generated through an endpoint. Generating API keys in the WordPress admin interface ​ To create or manage keys for a specific WordPress user, go to WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API. Note: Keys/Apps was found at WooCommerce > Settings > API > Key/Apps prior to WooCommerce 3.4. Click the "Add Key"

On this page Copy markdown Copies the current page content as markdown format to your clipboard WooCommerce (WC) 2.6+ is fully integrated with the WordPress REST API. This allows WC data to be created, read, updated, and deleted using requests in JSON format and using WordPress REST API Authentication methods and standard HTTP verbs which are understood by most HTTP clients. The current WP REST API integration version is v3 which takes a first-order position in endpoints. When WooPayments is active, it adds payment-specific endpoints under /wp-json/wc/v3/payments/ . Auth Methods
Zoho CRM supports OAuth 2.0 and API key authentication for its REST API endpoints.

Function. External systems call the Function by sending HTTP requests to this URL. The endpoint URL is unique per Function and follows Zoho's API domain pattern. Once enabled, the Function can receive HTTP requests and return HTTP responses, allowing it to serve as a lightweight API layer for your CRM logic. Authentication Options API Key (No Authentication) The endpoint URL serves as the authentication key. Anyone with the URL can invoke the Function, and no additional token or credential exchange is required. Best for: Inbound webhooks from third-party services, public data feeds, or trusted internal systems. Security note: REST API endpoints support OAuth 2.0 and API key authentication, which can be enabled or disabled independently.

Serverless Functions | Zoho CRM | Developer Tools
https://www.zoho.com/crm/developer/docs/functions/serverless.html

For production integrations, OAuth 2.0 is recommended. If you use an API key, treat it as a secret and avoid exposing it in client-side code or public repositories. For details on authentication methods, endpoint security, and API key management, refer to Serverless Endpoint Security . OAuth 2.0 (Authenticated Access) Requires the caller to obtain an access token via the standard OAuth 2.0 flow. The token is passed as a Bearer token in the Authorization header on every request. Best for: Partner integrations, user-scoped access, or any scenario where you need to verify the identity of the caller. 05 / Research architecture

The pipeline separates documentation discovery, structured extraction, verification and publication.

Application registry
→
Composio + Tavily
→
Document retrieval
→
Gemini researcher
→
Verification agent
→
SQLite + Report

01. Targeted discovery

Separate search queries investigate authentication, API access, capabilities and MCP implementations. Search execution uses the Composio SDK.

02. Passage grounding

Retrieved documents are divided into identifiable passages. The research agent references passage IDs instead of reproducing quotations.

03. Semantic verification

A separate model call evaluates claims and structured fields against the retrieved evidence. Unsupported values are conservatively removed.

04. Corrective research

Verification failures generate targeted follow-up queries. Candidate attempts are evaluated and the strongest result is selected.

05. Resumable execution

SQLite stores research results, attempt histories and execution status. Interrupted batches can resume without repeating completed applications.

06. Conservative publication

Unresolved fields remain unknown rather than being filled with unsupported assumptions.

06 / Engineering evaluation

Controlled pilot comparisons measure field completeness. Failed executions are excluded from matched comparisons and reported separately.

What changed?

V2 — Context optimization: Increasing and reorganizing research context did not consistently improve completeness.

V3 — Passage grounding: Replacing generated quotations with passage references improved evidence handling. One application encountered a service failure.

V4 — Verification resilience: Stricter classification instructions and transient-error retries produced the strongest three-application completeness benchmark.

07 / Limitations and next steps

Documentation-based assessment: API credentials and live business operations were not tested for every application.

Source coverage: Dynamic pages, inaccessible documentation and product naming ambiguity can limit research quality.

Verification limitations: Model-based semantic verification can miss factual errors and claim-to-field inconsistencies.

MCP discovery: A not-found classification indicates that research did not identify a relevant implementation. It does not establish that none exists.
